# Agent API: the Radio console

<!-- Generated by `npm run agent-api` from `src/ai/commands.js`. Do not edit by hand: `npm run check:agent-api` fails when this file is stale. -->

Registry version 1. Every command an AI engine or an agent may give the Radio console, with its arguments. The built-in model's prompt and answer schema, the online engines' tool definitions and the MCP tools are generated from the same registry (OpenSpec change `ai-assistant`, D0).

## How a command is applied

Each command is validated with the console's own rules (the reason a button shows in its tooltip) and applied through the same code path as the console button: it waits for its boundary in the queue and can be cancelled like a press. Nothing bypasses the console.

## Answer format

An engine answers with one JSON object: `note` (required, first: empty when the console can do the request, else one short sentence of what it cannot do) and `commands` (at most 4, in the order asked). Each command is an object with `kind` and only that kind's arguments. `track` is always one of the ids of the playing tracks the request lists.

```json
{"note":"","commands":[{"kind":"more","part":"arp"},{"kind":"darker"}]}
```

## Commands

| Kind | Button | What it does | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `energy-up` | ▲ More energy | raise the energy of the rest of the song | none |
| `energy-down` | ▼ Less energy | lower the energy of the rest of the song | none |
| `more-complex` | More complex | more tracks at once | none |
| `less-complex` | Less complex | fewer tracks at once (simpler) | none |
| `more` | + (instrument) | one more track of an instrument | `part`: `kick`, `beat`, `bass`, `arp`, `hook`, `guitar`, `pad`, `texture`, an instrument of the console (hook is the melody, beat the drums other than the kick) |
| `less` | − (instrument) | one fewer track of an instrument | `part`: `kick`, `beat`, `bass`, `arp`, `hook`, `guitar`, `pad`, `texture`, an instrument of the console (hook is the melody, beat the drums other than the kick) |
| `lock-part` | Lock (instrument) | the director stops changing an instrument | `part`: `kick`, `beat`, `bass`, `arp`, `hook`, `guitar`, `pad`, `texture`, `riser`, an instrument of the console, or the riser |
| `unlock-part` | Unlock (instrument) | the director may change the instrument again | `part`: `kick`, `beat`, `bass`, `arp`, `hook`, `guitar`, `pad`, `texture`, `riser`, an instrument of the console, or the riser |
| `riser` | Riser | a rising noise sweep into the next part change | `bars` (optional): `auto`, `2`, `4`, `8`, its length in bars, or auto; `dir` (optional): `up`, `down`, up (rising) or down (falling) |
| `pattern` | Add a saved pattern | one of the listener's saved patterns, by name: without track as a new track, with track in place of that playing track | `name`: string, the saved pattern's name as the listener wrote it; `track` (optional): string, the id of a playing track |
| `voicing` | Part harmony | how a part sits on the chords | `type`: `lead`, `bass`, `arp`, `pad`, `guitar`, a part: lead (the melody or the guitar), bass, arp, pad, guitar; `treatment`: `thirds`, `octave`, `colour`, `inversion`, `auto`, thirds, octave, colour (chord colour), inversion, or auto |
| `vary` | Vary | new notes for a part | `type`: `lead`, `bass`, `arp`, `pad`, `guitar`, a part: lead (the melody or the guitar), bass, arp, pad, guitar |
| `swap` | Swap | another ready-made part for a part | `type`: `lead`, `bass`, `arp`, `pad`, `guitar`, a part: lead (the melody or the guitar), bass, arp, pad, guitar |
| `darker` | Darker | close the filters | none |
| `brighter` | Brighter | open the filters | none |
| `dirtier` | Dirtier | more drive and distortion | none |
| `cleaner` | Cleaner | less drive and fewer effects | none |
| `more-space` | More space | more delay and reverb | none |
| `instrument` | Change instrument | another sound for the leading instrument, or for track | `track` (optional): string, the id of a playing track |
| `progression` | Change chords | other chords (a new chord progression) | none |
| `key` | Change key | change key: up or down a fifth, to the relative key, or auto | `to` (optional): `auto`, `up`, `down`, `relative`, up and down: a fifth; relative: the relative major or minor; auto |
| `talk-more` | Narrator more | the narrator comments more | none |
| `talk-less` | Narrator less | the narrator comments less | none |
| `say-live` | Say now | the voice track speaks a line now, at most 12 words | `text`: string, the line to say, as the listener wrote it |
| `drop` | Drop | jump to the drop | none |
| `stay` | Stay | repeat the part playing once more | none |
| `extend` | Extend | make the song longer before its ending | none |
| `end` | End | go to the outro and end the song | none |
| `volume` | Volume | set the volume of a track: value from 0 to 1.2 (0.5 is half) | `track`: string, the id of a playing track; `value`: number, the new volume, 0 to 1.2 |
| `mute` | Mute | mute a playing track | `track`: string, the id of a playing track |
| `unmute` | Back | a muted track plays again | `track`: string, the id of a playing track |
| `lock` | Lock track | the director stops changing a track | `track`: string, the id of a playing track |
| `unlock` | Unlock track | the director may change a track again | `track`: string, the id of a playing track |

## Left out

- `add`: legacy, kept for sessions recorded before the per-instrument console.
- `sound`: a sound rolled on the page by the track card's dice: its values come from the page, the assistant asks for instrument.
- `remove`: legacy, kept for sessions recorded before the per-instrument console.
- `voice`: a preset form, not a single request.
- `voice-sound`: a preset form, not a single request.
- `curve`: drawn values on the curves.
- `curve-reset`: drawn values on the curves.

## Guards

- **Pattern names.** `name` is free text. The app matches it against the saved patterns that fit the song: case, accents, punctuation and filler words ignored, exact first, then a fuzzy score per word with a threshold of 0.75. No match, or two matches within 0.05, is rejected with a clear message.
- **Cannot.** These requests are answered "cannot" before any engine is asked: change the tempo; change the time signature; play the song backwards.
- **Vague requests.** A request that names no command word, instrument, playing track or saved pattern is shown as a proposal before anything applies.
- **The pattern the request names.** A `pattern` command is kept when at least 60 % of its name's words appear in the request. Otherwise the app uses the saved pattern the request itself names (in quotes, after or before "pattern", or every word of a name), rejects the request's name when no saved pattern matches it, or shows the answer as a proposal.
- **The command the request names.** When the request uses a word that belongs to exactly one command and the answer has neither that command nor a close one, or the request names a saved pattern in full and the answer has no pattern, the answer is shown as a proposal.
- **Spoken lines.** A request to say, speak or announce a line, with the line after a colon or in quotes, becomes `say-live` with that line without asking an engine.

## Tools

Online engines get one tool per command, named `console_<kind>` with `-` as `_` (for example `console_energy_up`), whose input schema is the command's arguments. The MCP server's tools have the same names, descriptions and schemas (`inputSchema`).
